Subject: Initial proposal on IP indemnity (MSA redlines attached)

Jake — attaching a clean redline for the MSA/Order Form focused on the IP/3rd-party infringement sections. Quick summary of our proposed compromise:

- Insurance-first approach: require customer to exhaust primary insurance for IP claims, Redwood will step in after insurance exhaustion.
- Cap on Redwood liability for IP infringement tied to the order form value (propose 3x ARR, minimum $1M, maximum $5M) — open to negotiation.
- Redwood to control defense but with consultation obligations and approval carve-outs for settlements > $250,000.
- Evidence & notice timelines: 14-day initial notice window; customer to provide claim specifics and sample outputs; we propose an evidence template to make triage efficient.

Attachments: redlines_draft_v3.docx (docx) — public redline; evidence_template.xlsx (xls) — suggested evidence checklist.

Rishi — thanks for the quick turnaround and the templates. Our legal team reviewed and has a few sticking points they asked me to surface:

1) Defense control — Novacorp is uncomfortable with unilateral vendor control for IP third-party claims. We typically insist on either (a) customer control, or (b) joint control with right to independent counsel if a conflict arises.
2) Settlement approvals — your $250k threshold is fine but we want clearer guardrails around who signs off and what constitutes an acceptable settlement (no admission of liability without consent).
3) Evidence burden — we need a practical minimum of what you require for initial triage. Full datasets or logs may not be shareable; can we accept redacted samples plus a verification checklist?
4) Cap — we can discuss $1M-$5M ranges but our procurement aims for higher insurance-backed limits.

Attached: novacorp_redlines.pdf (pdf) — their redlines with comments. Can Kim weigh in on defense-control alternatives that preserve our ability to run the defense while addressing their governance ask?

Jake

Rishi / Ben — quick legal take (high level) and suggested compromise language we can present to Novacorp: 

1) Defense control: propose vendor-led defense (Redwood) with an express requirement to keep Novacorp reasonably informed and provide opportunity to participate. If a conflict arises or Redwood elects not to defend, Novacorp may assume control. That addresses their governance ask while preserving operational efficiency.

2) Settlement approvals: add an approval clause for settlements that involve non-monetary terms or admission of liability; for monetary settlements, require written consent for amounts > $250,000. We can concede to a lower threshold for procurement roadblock reasons — consider $100,000 if Ben advises it's necessary.

3) Insurance-first + cap: recommend 'insurance-first' language with Redwood's exposure capped at the higher of (a) $1,000,000 or (b) 3x the fees paid under the applicable order form, up to a $5,000,000 maximum. We should also include an explicit insurance-offset/credit clause (i.e., payments from insurance reduce Redwood's cap).

4) Evidence template: we should accept redacted outputs and a small sample (<= 500 tokens or representative snippets) plus metadata (timestamp, prompt hash, model name, route id). Avoid asking for full datasets or customer PII. Request a protective agreement for any sensitive materials.

5) Operational SLA for notice and triage: 14-day initial notice, 30-day evidence handoff window after notice, and prioritized engineering support for reproducing the issue.

Attachments: redwood_legal_response_2028-03-30.docx (docx) — full suggested clause language and an evidence_template.xlsx (xls) we can send to them.

If Ben thinks the commercial thresholds need to move to get procurement unblocked, propose target numbers and I'll draft the counter redline. If we need exec escalation, Marissa can weigh in on exceptions.

Kim

Subject: Counter: Redwood position on defense control, cap, and evidence handoff

Jake — appreciate the detailed feedback. After conferring with legal and commercial, here's the counter we can take to your counsel this afternoon: 

- Defense: Redwood will lead the defense (vendor-led) but will provide Novacorp with notice, weekly updates during active litigation, and the right to participate with counsel at Novacorp's expense. If Redwood declines to defend or there's a direct conflict, Novacorp may assume control.
- Settlements: Redwood will not settle any claim that admits liability or imposes non-monetary obligations on Novacorp without prior written consent. Monetary settlements require Novacorp's consent for amounts > $250,000.
- Insurance-first & cap: Customer's primary insurance pays first. Redwood's residual exposure will be the greater of $1,000,000 or 3x fees paid under the affected order form, not exceeding $5,000,000. Insurance recoveries offset Redwood's cap.
- Evidence: we accept redacted samples (representative snippets), metadata (prompt hash, model, timestamp), and a short reproduction checklist. Sensitive data must be shared under an agreed protective addendum — we've attached a template.
- Timeline / MAP: propose a 7-business-day window for Novacorp to confirm acceptance of this counter or request a 30-min sync with Kim. If we can't land terms within two weeks, we'll route to procurement for escalation.

Attachments: counter_offer_redlines.docx (docx) — redline showing proposed edits side-by-side; evidence_template.xlsx (xls) — trimmed to the fields we require.

If that's acceptable, I'll send this formally to legal@novacorp.com and ask for their markups. Ben / Marissa — flag if we need to adjust thresholds before I send.

Thanks,
